Explanation of the words:

"لا تحرك به لسانك" (Do not move your tongue with it): i.e., do not move your tongue with the Qur'an before Jibril has finished reciting it.

"لتعجل به" (to hasten with it): i.e., out of fear that it might slip away from you.

"إن علينا جمعه" (Indeed, upon Us is its collection): i.e., in your breast.

"وقرآنه" (and its recitation): i.e., your recitation of it, such that We make it flow upon your tongue.

"فإذا قرأناه" (So when We recite it): i.e., when Jibril recites it to you.

"فاتبع قرآنه" (then follow its recitation): i.e., listen to its recitation.

"ثم إن علينا بيانه" (Then indeed upon Us is its explanation): i.e., for you, by making you understand what of its meanings is difficult for you.

"كلا" (No!): i.e., the matter is not as you claim, that there is no resurrection and no recompense.

"يحبون العاجلة" (They love the hastening [world]): i.e., the present world, so they work for it.

"ويذرون الآخرة" (and leave behind the Hereafter): i.e., and they abandon the Hereafter, so they do not work for it.

"ناضرة" (radiant): i.e., beautiful and luminous.

"إلى ربها ناظرة" (looking at its Lord): i.e., looking at Allah, the Exalted, its Lord, without being veiled from Him.

"باسرة" (scowling): i.e., gloomy, darkened, frowning.

"تظن" (expects): i.e., is certain.

"أن يفعل بها فاقرة" (that a calamity will be inflicted upon it): i.e., a great catastrophe that breaks the spine.

Meaning of the verses:

When Allah, the Exalted, censured those who turn away from the Qur'an and deny it and the Resurrection and recompense, He mentioned in these verses those who turn toward the Qur'an and hasten to receive it, so the connection between these verses and what precedes them is one of contrast. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 75, verse 26–40:

Explanation of the words:

"Idha balaghat" (when it reaches): i.e., the soul (al-nafs).

"Al-taraqi" (the collarbones): plural of taraqwa, i.e., the bones of the throat.

"Wa qila man raq" (and it is said, "Who will heal him?"): i.e., and those around him, his visitors or his nurses, said, "Is there anyone who can perform ruqya (spiritual incantation) on him so that he may be healed?"

"Wa zanna annahu al-firaq" (and he is certain that it is parting): i.e., he becomes certain that it is parting from the world, because the soul has reached the throat.

"Wa iltafa al-saq bi al-saq" (and leg is entwined with leg): i.e., one of his legs became entwined with the other, or the severity of parting from the world became entwined with the severity of the approach of the Hereafter and its terrors.

"Ila rabbika yawma'idhin al-masaq" (to your Lord, on that Day, is the driving): i.e., when the soul reaches the throat, it is driven to its Lord and Creator to receive its recompense.

"Fala saddaqa wa la salla" (So he did not affirm, nor did he pray): i.e., the human being who thinks that God will never gather his bones did not affirm (the truth) and did not pray.

"Wa lakin kadhdhaba" (But he denied): i.e., the Qur'an.

"Wa tawalla" (and turned away): i.e., from faith.

"Yatamatta" (he swaggered): i.e., he strutted in his gait, out of self-admiration.

"Awla laka" (woe to you): i.e., may what you dislike befall you, O one who admires himself and denies the meeting with his Lord.

"Fa-awla" (so woe to you): i.e., it is more fitting for you.

"Thumma awla laka fa-awla" (then again, woe to you, so woe to you): i.e., may what you dislike befall you a second time, so woe to you, it is more fitting for you too.

"An yutraka sudan" (that he would be left neglected): i.e., left without obligation in this world and without reckoning, and without being recompensed in the Hereafter.

"Tumna" (it was ejaculated): i.e., poured into the womb.

"Fa-khalaqa fa-sawwa" (then He created and proportioned): i.e., God created man from it and proportioned him by balancing his limbs.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to establish the belief in resurrection and recompense. His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Kalla﴾ (No!), means: the matter is not as you suppose, O human, that God will not gather your bones, nor give you life, nor recompense you. Look at yourself, as you lie on your deathbed: to where will your being driven when your soul reaches your collarbones, the bones of your throat, and your visitors and nurses say, "Is there anyone who can perform ruqya on him, or a physician who can treat him?" And you become certain that it is parting from your worldly life, your family and your kin. And your right leg is entwined with your left, and the severity of parting from the world is entwined with the severity of your turning toward the Hereafter. Here, look to where you are taken: as for your body, it goes to its resting place in the earth, where it will be concealed; as for your soul, it goes to your Lord to judge concerning you. You had denied His signs and disbelieved in His blessings. ﴿Fala saddaqa wa la salla﴾ (So you did not affirm, nor did you pray). Rather, you denied and turned away; this was your share of your religion. As for your worldly life, you used to swagger in arrogance and strut in self-admiration. Then ﴿Awla laka fa-awla﴾ (Woe to you, and woe to you again), meaning: may ruin befall you in this world; ﴿Thumma awla laka fa-awla﴾ (then again, woe to you, and woe to you), meaning: may punishment befall you in the Hereafter. And it is a return to your rebuke and reproach, O you who disbelieved your Lord and disowned your origin: listen to what is said to you. Do you think you will be left neglected, living aimlessly, not commanded and not forbidden, nothing taken from you and nothing given? ﴿Kalla﴾ (No!). Did you not, before your disbelief and denial, become a drop of fluid, a drop of water from semen that was ejaculated? Say, "Yes," or, "Woe to you, and woe to you." Then you became a clinging clot, and God, majestic is His majesty, created you from it and proportioned your creation by balancing your limbs, and made of your kind the male and the female. Tell me, by your Lord, do you deny this? If you say no, we say: is not God able to give life to the dead? Glory be to You, O God, indeed (He is able).

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The legitimacy of ruqya if it is by the Qur'an or by good words.

2- Emphasis on the matter of zakat and prayer, obligatory and voluntary.

3- The prohibition of conceit, pride, and swaggering in walking.

4- Establishing the belief in resurrection and recompense.

5- Man was not created in vain, and the whole universe likewise.

6- The legitimacy of saying "Glory be to You, O God, indeed (He is able)" for whoever recites or hears this verse, whether imam or follower, and it is ﴿Is not He who is able to give life to the dead?﴾
